problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}6y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A
$$

given that the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane is given by

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1-x,\,0\le x\le 1}.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals Over Type III Regions

feedback.problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{4}6x\,dy]dA,
$$

Evaluate the repeated integral above given that $D$ is a region in the $xz$-plane bounded by the lines $z=0,$ $x=0,$ and the curve $z+{x}^{2}=4.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{4}6x\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}6x[y]_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=4}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}6x(4-{x}^{2})\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}24x-6{x}^{3}\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to calculate this double integral, we plot $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xz$-plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/612c4fda39f7003024c322b6d1fa5c279815923905c8d023547a3be6b4a6805a.png)

Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $z$ and then with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}24x-6{x}^{3}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4-{x}^{2}}24x-6{x}^{3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(24x-6{x}^{3})[z]_{z=0}^{z=4-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(24x-6{x}^{3})(4-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}96x-48{x}^{3}+6{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[48{x}^{2}-12{x}^{4}+{x}^{6}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(192-192+64)-0 \\  & =64\end{aligned}
$$
